decisive_items: Few, micro-ischemic focal lesions in the periventricular and deep white matter of the cerebral hemispheres
Mild cerebral atrophy/aging more pronounced in the curvatures of the cerebral hemispheres
The patient's main difficulties were noted on his left side.
response.rationale: MRI shows micro-ischemic white matter lesions and cerebral atrophy, classic for cerebral small vessel disease, with left-sided symptoms and comorbid depression/anxiety as common accompaniments. Broader cerebrovascular disease is less specific, while vascular dementia is not established because MMSE improved after treatment and functional decline is not described.

rejected.why: No ventriculomegaly or classic NPH triad; empty sella is nonspecific.
Cognitive score improved after treatment and no dementia-level functional decline is documented.
Does not account for MRI micro-ischemic lesions or left-sided focal symptoms.
No subdural collection, trauma, or mass effect; imaging shows atrophy and ischemic lesions.
Mood symptoms are comorbid but do not explain MRI lesions or left-sided deficits.
Anxiety alone cannot explain cognitive, motor, or imaging findings.
Too broad; imaging pattern is vascular/ischemic rather than a specific neurodegenerative signature.
Psychiatric symptoms are secondary/comorbid and do not explain the MRI findings.
Leg pain alone does not explain brain MRI abnormalities or cognitive/mood symptoms.
